analysis.title: Americas Consumer Products: HPC NielsenIQ Data thru 10/17 highlights slight deceleration in L4wk sales growth
key_insights: NielsenIQ data for the week ending 10/17/26 shows HPC (household and personal care) sales growth slowed to +3.8% in the latest 4 weeks from +4.4% last month, with a larger moderation on a 2-year stacked basis.
The YoY slowdown came from sequentially lower pricing, partly offset by higher volume growth versus last month. Sales on promotion fell 110bps YoY.
KMB led the group with double-digit sales growth. Volume growth was strong, while price declines were larger sequentially as price investments accelerated.
CHD, CL and KVUE posted modest sequential acceleration in sales growth. CHD and KVUE were mainly volume-led. CL was mainly price-led, with volumes up only slightly.
PG posted solid sales growth but slowed sequentially in both volume and pricing. PG leads the group over the latest 2 weeks with mid-single-digit growth.
CLX lagged the group with sales declines over the latest 4 weeks (-1.1%), though trends improved modestly from last month.
Over the latest 2 weeks, sales growth broadly accelerated versus the prior 2 weeks for all the companies named above.
Personal care $ sales grew +3.6% over 4 weeks, led by adult incontinence, tissue, deodorant and soap. Volumes rose +8.8%, led by tissue. Branded volumes were +13.5% and private label volumes -0.8%.

Beauty $ sales rose +6.2% over 4 weeks, led by skin care (+8.4%) and aided by fragrances and color cosmetics. Beauty volumes were +4.6%, with color cosmetics +19.4% and fragrances +11.7%. Branded volumes were +5.3% and private label +0.3%.
Home care sales grew +2.9% over 4 weeks on +2.0% volume growth. OTC sales rose +5.5%, with branded trends outpacing private label, which declined.

KMB gained the most volume share in facial tissue (+830bps) and dry toilet tissue (+170bps). It lost share in training pants (-460bps), disposable diapers (-290bps), wet toilet tissue (-280bps), sanitary napkins (-230bps) and tampons (-90bps). KMB promo sales were down -10bps YoY.

In the diaper category, PG Pampers volume rose +10.2% over 4 weeks and PG gained 217bps of dollar share. KMB Huggies sales fell -7.8% and it lost 276bps of dollar share. Zuru and Millie Moon grew over 20%.
In dry toilet tissue, KMB (Scott, Cottonelle) sales rose +9.8% over 4 weeks with +14.4% volume and -4.6% price. PG Charmin sales rose +0.2% and lost 116bps of dollar share.
In liquid laundry detergent, Tide 4-week sales rose +2.5% with volume +0.8%. Church & Dwight (Arm & Hammer) sales rose +5.9% and gained 31bps of dollar share.

CLX gained volume share in liquid salad dressing (+170bps) and pre-moistened cleaning wipes (+30bps). It lost share in detergent boosters, charcoal, multi-purpose cleaners and cat litter. CLX promo sales were down -360bps YoY.
CHD gained volume share in stain removers (+280bps), mouthwash (+260bps) and laundry detergent (+130bps). It lost share in contraceptives (-380bps). CHD promo sales were down -360bps YoY.
PG gained volume share in disposable diapers (+320bps), dish soap (+140bps) and auto dish detergent (+140bps). It lost share in paper towels (-290bps) and liquid laundry detergent (-120bps).

CL gained volume share in hand soaps (+450bps) and liquid fabric softeners (+80bps). It lost share in toothbrush (-220bps), toothpaste (-110bps) and body wash (-50bps). CL promo sales were up +90bps YoY, the only company here with higher promo.
KVUE gained volume share in bandages (+330bps) and pain relief (+190bps). It lost share in face cosmetics (-50bps) and GI care (-30bps). KVUE promo sales were down -80bps YoY.
Private label dollar share fell YoY in most personal care categories over 4 weeks. Private label share rose in color cosmetics and paper products.

sector_views.rationale: Latest 4-week HPC sales growth slowed to +3.8% from +4.4%. Pricing was lower and volume growth higher, with a broad pickup in the latest 2 weeks.

earnings_insights: Third-quarter organic sales backtests for CHD, CL, CLX, KMB, KVUE, PG, EPC, ENR and REYN compare NielsenIQ dollar sales growth against reported or GS-estimated figures. Quarterly figures are only shown in charts and are not stated in the text.
risk_factors: Pricing is turning negative or lower sequentially in the group (HPC price -0.5% in the latest 4 weeks), with KMB investing in price.
The 2-year stacked sales growth trend is moderating more than the 1-year trend.
CLX sales continue to decline over 4 weeks (-1.1%), with velocity declines the main driver.
Private label share gains in some categories, and promo intensity changes, could shift the volume mix.
